_comment: Mail flag → routing contracts. Spine for the Mail-flag pipeline.
Keyed by Mail's `flag index` (integer 0..6). Apple Mail's default
color order is rainbow-style — typical mapping is:
BUT this varies; verify with `mail-flag-worker --probe` after flagging
name             — human label, becomes the Processed/<Name> mailbox
enabled          — bool; false = ignore this color
eml_dest         — where to drop the full .eml
body_md_dest     — where to drop the converted body markdown
url_action       — script to call per URL in body (omit/null = skip)
attachments      — map of extension (or space-sep list, or '*' fallback)
processed_mailbox — Mail mailbox name to move msg to on success
Add a color = fill in a slot. The worker reads this file on every run.

1.name: FreeEnergy
1._comment: VERIFIED 2026-05-26: Esa flagged a test message 'purple' in Mail UI and SQLite recorded flag_color=1. So slot 1 IS purple = Free Energy on this machine.
1._clear_flag_comment: Default false: keep the Purple flag as category metadata even in Processed/FreeEnergy. The folder location is the routing-state signal. Set true if you prefer 'flagged=pending, unflagged=done' semantics.

5.name: Unknown-5
5._comment: Color identity unknown. 566 existing messages have flag_color=5; not yet mapped to a UI color. Run mail-flag-worker --probe after flagging one message of each remaining UI color.
